newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Cavallo to Brazil: Don't fear the Tango effect.
newsitem.headline: Cavallo to Brazil: Don't fear the Tango effect.

text.p: Former Argentine Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo said Argentina was quickly emerging from an 18 month recession and would soon become a fast- growing and vigorous trading partner for Brazil.
"Don't be afraid of a Tango effect or anything like it," Cavallo told an audience of bankers in Sao Paulo.

"In the next few years you will see extraordinary growth in Argentina...you will have a fast-growing neighbor and a vigorous trading partner," he said. Cavallo cited recent growth rates as showing Argentina had overcome the worst of a recession triggered by the 1994 Mexican currency crisis.
He predicted that new legislation designed to encourage savings, would fund a construction boom that would help bring unemployment down from over 18 percent.
Cavallo said Brazil and Argentina, the two senior partners in the four-country Mercosur trade pact, should seek new ways to strengthen the budding customs union.
He criticized the Brazilian government for blocking Argentine banks from opening subsidiaries in Brazil adding that Brazilian bankers should not worry about the competition.
"The Brazilian finance industry is far more sophisticated and has invested more in high technology than its Argentine counterparts. You have nothing to be afraid of," Cavallo said.

Asked if Brazil could continue to delay the deregulation of its oil and energy industry, Cavallo thought that was highly unlikely. He said Argentina had been right in choosing to dismantle its oil and power monopolies and was now enjoying the benefits of cheaper energy prices.
"If Argentina's energy prices are cheaper than Brazil's, new energy intensive investment opportunities will move to Argentina instead of Brazil and that is something you will never allow," he added.
